themeHint: Think stars and stripes, Hollywood and New York.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: American astronaut who took 'one small step' onto the Moon in 1969.
clues.fact: Neil Armstrong was a US Navy pilot before he became an astronaut.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Big toothy reptile of Florida's swamps, a cousin of the crocodile with a wider snout.
clues.fact: The American alligator is the official state reptile of Florida.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: The largest US state, bought from Russia in 1867.
clues.fact: Alaska is the largest US state by area, more than twice the size of Texas.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Flying machine the Wright brothers first flew in 1903; you board one with a ticket and a passport.
clues.fact: The Wright brothers' first powered flight in 1903 lasted only about 12 seconds.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Pastry dessert in the saying 'as American as...', filled with the fruit that keeps the doctor away.
clues.fact: Apple pie recipes were written down in England centuries before the United States existed.

clues.label: Award
clues.clue: Hollywood's biggest film prize, a gold statuette nicknamed the Oscar (formal name, two words).
clues.fact: The first Academy Awards ceremony was held in 1929.

themeHint: Waves, salt water and ships: what covers most of the planet.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Disney's Little Mermaid, a red-haired princess who longs to live on land.
clues.fact: The Little Mermaid is based on a fairy tale by Danish author Hans Christian Andersen.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Giant seabird with the widest wings of any bird, gliding over oceans for days.
clues.fact: The wandering albatross has the largest wingspan of any living bird, over 3 metres.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Ocean whose waves roll onto Lagos beaches, and the beaches of Brazil on the other side.
clues.fact: The Atlantic is the second-largest ocean on Earth, after the Pacific.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Heavy hooked object dropped overboard to stop a ship drifting.
clues.fact: The earliest anchors were simply heavy stones tied to a rope.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Tiny, very salty silver fish, often sold in tins and laid on pizzas.
clues.fact: Anchovies are small fish that swim in huge schools.

clues.label: Job
clues.clue: Highest rank in a navy, held by Britain's Lord Nelson; this officer commands a whole fleet.
clues.fact: Horatio Nelson was a British admiral famous for winning the Battle of Trafalgar in 1805.

themeHint: Tea, rain and red phone boxes.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: England football star who married a Spice Girl.
clues.fact: David Beckham played for Manchester United, Real Madrid and LA Galaxy, among others.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Stocky, wrinkly dog breed that is a symbol of British toughness.
clues.fact: Bulldogs were originally bred in England for the cruel sport of bull-baiting.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Famous bell in the clock tower beside the Houses of Parliament in London.
clues.fact: Big Ben is officially the name of the great bell; the tower is called the Elizabeth Tower.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Red double-decker that carries passengers around London; you wait at a stop for one.
clues.fact: London's red double-decker buses are a world-famous symbol of the city.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: British pub meal of sausages on creamy whipped potato with onion gravy (three words).
clues.fact: Sausages got the nickname 'bangers' because they can burst with a bang when fried.

clues.label: Music
clues.clue: Famous Liverpool band of John, Paul, George and Ringo, who sang Hey Jude.
clues.fact: The Beatles are widely regarded as the best-selling music act of all time.

themeHint: Think of the Taj Mahal's home country.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Lazy, fun-loving bear who sings 'The Bare Necessities' in Disney's The Jungle Book.
clues.fact: The Jungle Book's author, Rudyard Kipling, was born in Bombay (now Mumbai) in 1865.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Striped big cat that is India's national animal, named after a region in the east.
clues.fact: The Bengal tiger is the national animal of India.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Old name, used until 1995, for Mumbai, India's biggest city.
clues.fact: The city officially changed its name from Bombay to Mumbai in 1995.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Small decorative dot, often red, worn on the forehead between the eyebrows.
clues.fact: A bindi can be a simple red dot or a sparkly stick-on jewel.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Fragrant spiced rice dish layered with meat or vegetables.
clues.fact: The city of Hyderabad is famous for its own style of this rice dish.

clues.label: Film
clues.clue: Nickname of the Hindi-language film industry based in Mumbai.
clues.fact: India produces more films each year than any other country.

themeHint: The coldest season of the year.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Santa's surname; he delivers presents on a cold Christmas Eve.
clues.fact: The name Santa Claus comes from the Dutch Sinterklaas, based on Saint Nicholas.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: North American name for the reindeer, which roams the freezing Arctic in huge herds.
clues.fact: Caribou and reindeer are the same species.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Huge snowy country north of the USA with a maple leaf on its flag.
clues.fact: Canada has the longest coastline of any country in the world.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Warm outer garment you button up before going out into the snow.
clues.fact: Down coats are filled with the soft under-feathers of ducks or geese.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Hot chocolate drink for a frosty day; Ghana and Ivory Coast grow most of its beans.
clues.fact: Most of the world's cocoa beans are grown in West Africa, with Ivory Coast and Ghana the biggest producers.

clues.label: Sport
clues.clue: Winter Olympic ice sport where players sweep the ice in front of a sliding granite stone.
clues.fact: Many curling stones are made from granite quarried on Ailsa Craig, an island off Scotland.

themeHint: Think saloons, sheriffs, horses and tumbleweeds in 1800s America.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: ___ Eastwood, squinting star of cowboy films like The Good, the Bad and the Ugly.
clues.fact: Clint Eastwood won Best Director Oscars for Unforgiven and Million Dollar Baby.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Wild dog of the prairies, famous for howling at night.
clues.fact: Coyotes live across North America, even in big cities.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Sunny US state where the 1849 Gold Rush drew thousands of prospectors; home of Hollywood.
clues.fact: Gold was discovered at Sutter's Mill in California in 1848.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Canvas-topped wooden cart pulled by oxen or horses, carrying settlers across the prairie.
clues.fact: Covered wagons were nicknamed 'prairie schooners' because their white tops looked like sails.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Spicy Texan stew of beef, beans and hot peppers, also called ___ con carne.
clues.fact: Chili con carne is the official state dish of Texas.

clues.label: Job
clues.clue: Ranch worker on horseback who herds cattle and wears a wide-brimmed hat.
clues.fact: Many of the first American cowboys learned their skills from Mexican vaqueros.

themeHint: Kangaroos, koalas and the Sydney Opera House.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Naturalist famous for the theory of evolution; Australia's tropical northern city is named after him.
clues.fact: Charles Darwin visited Australia in 1836 during his voyage aboard HMS Beagle.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Wild yellow dog of the Outback.
clues.fact: Dingoes rarely bark; they communicate mostly by howling.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Dry, sandy land that covers much of the Outback, such as the Great Victoria or the Simpson.
clues.fact: Australia is the driest inhabited continent on Earth.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Long wooden wind instrument played by Aboriginal people, with a deep droning sound.
clues.fact: Didgeridoos are traditionally made from tree trunks hollowed out by termites.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Simple campfire bread of flour, water and salt baked in hot ashes; rhymes with 'camper'.
clues.fact: Damper was traditionally made by stockmen with little more than flour, water and salt.

clues.label: Money
clues.clue: Australia's currency, which shares its name with America's money.
clues.fact: Australia replaced its pound with its own dollar in 1966.

themeHint: Think Berlin, beer halls and the autobahn.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Rudolf ___, German engineer whose engine, and the fuel it burns, carry his surname.
clues.fact: Rudolf Diesel was born in Paris to German parents.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Long, low 'sausage dog' bred in Germany to chase badgers down holes.
clues.fact: The name Dachshund means 'badger dog' in German.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Ruhr city whose yellow-and-black football club, Borussia, plays in front of a giant terrace.
clues.fact: Borussia Dortmund's stadium has a huge standing terrace nicknamed the Yellow Wall.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Germany's money before the euro replaced it in 2002 (two words, the first meaning 'German').
clues.fact: Deutsche Mark notes and coins were replaced by the euro in 2002.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Spit-roasted meat in flatbread, a favourite late-night street food in Berlin.
clues.fact: The doner kebab sandwich became hugely popular in Berlin thanks to Turkish immigrants.

clues.label: Language
clues.clue: What the locals call their own language.
clues.fact: German is the most widely spoken native language in the European Union.

themeHint: Crowns, thrones, palaces and kings and queens.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: British queen who reigned for 70 years until 2022.
clues.fact: Queen Elizabeth II was the longest-reigning British monarch in history.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Biggest of the flightless birds of Antarctica, named after a royal title even higher than king.
clues.fact: Male emperor penguins keep their eggs warm on their feet through the Antarctic winter.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Scottish capital with a famous castle on a hill and a royal palace, Holyroodhouse.
clues.fact: The Palace of Holyroodhouse is the monarch's official residence in Scotland.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: King Arthur's legendary magic sword.
clues.fact: In some versions of the legend, Excalibur was given to King Arthur by the Lady of the Lake.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Black tea flavoured with bergamot orange, named after a British nobleman who was prime minister.
clues.fact: Earl Grey tea gets its flavour from oil of the bergamot orange.

clues.label: Title
clues.clue: Female ruler of an empire.
clues.fact: Queen Victoria was also given the title Empress of India.

themeHint: Feathers, beaks and wings: creatures that fly (mostly).

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: 'The Eagle', the plucky British ski jumper of the 1988 Olympics, later played by Taron Egerton.
clues.fact: Eddie 'the Eagle' Edwards finished last at the Calgary Olympics but became a crowd favourite.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Tall Australian bird that cannot fly.
clues.fact: The emu is the second-tallest bird in the world after the ostrich.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: South American country on the equator that owns the Galapagos, home of Darwin's finches.
clues.fact: The Galapagos Islands belong to Ecuador, and the equator passes through the country.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Old word for a puffy duvet, first stuffed with the soft feathers of a northern sea duck.
clues.fact: Eider ducks line their nests with their own soft down, which is collected for bedding.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Laid by hens and eaten boiled, fried or scrambled.
clues.fact: A hen's egg can have a white or brown shell depending on the breed of hen.

clues.label: Sport
clues.clue: Nigeria's national football team are the Super ___, named after a big bird of prey.
clues.fact: The Super Eagles have won the Africa Cup of Nations three times: 1980, 1994 and 2013.

themeHint: Hot, bright and smoky: think matches, candles and bonfires.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Guy ___, who tried to blow up Parliament in 1605; Britain lights bonfires every 5 November.
clues.fact: Bonfire Night on 5 November marks the failed Gunpowder Plot of 1605.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Flying beetle whose tail glows in the dark on summer nights.
clues.fact: Fireflies make light through a chemical reaction called bioluminescence.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Japan's tallest mountain, a snow-capped volcano near Tokyo.
clues.fact: Mount Fuji last erupted in 1707.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Hard grey stone struck against steel to make sparks; Stone Age people made tools from it.
clues.fact: Early humans used this stone both to make sharp tools and to start fires.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Cooking trick where brandy is poured over a dish and set alight right at the table.
clues.fact: Crepes Suzette is a French dessert famously set alight before serving.

clues.label: Job
clues.clue: Brave worker who sprays water on blazes and rescues people.
clues.fact: Ancient Rome had organised firefighting teams called the Vigiles.

themeHint: Think of things that go very, very quickly, like racing cars.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Enzo ___, founder of Italy's famous red racing cars with a prancing horse badge.
clues.fact: The company's logo shows a black prancing horse.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Bird of prey; its diving peregrine kind is the fastest animal on Earth.
clues.fact: A diving peregrine falcon can reach speeds of over 300 km/h.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Nordic land of lakes and saunas, capital Helsinki; F1 champions Hakkinen and Raikkonen came from here.
clues.fact: Finland has produced several F1 world champions, including Mika Hakkinen and Kimi Raikkonen.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Fast military plane built for air combat, like the F-16 or Top Gun's F-14.
clues.fact: Many modern combat aircraft can fly faster than the speed of sound.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Burgers and fries served in minutes at a drive-through.
clues.fact: The first McDonald's restaurant opened in California in 1940.

clues.label: Sport
clues.clue: Top motor-racing series with Grand Prix races around the world.
clues.fact: The first Formula One World Championship race was held at Silverstone in 1950.

themeHint: Precious, shiny and yellow: think of first-place medals.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Fairy-tale girl who ate the three bears' porridge and found one bowl 'just right'.
clues.fact: In early versions of the story, the intruder was an old woman, not a little girl.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Orange pet fish often kept in a round bowl.
clues.fact: Goldfish were first domesticated in China over a thousand years ago.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: West African country once called the Gold Coast; its capital is Accra.
clues.fact: In 1957 Ghana became one of the first sub-Saharan African countries to gain independence.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Shiny brick of precious metal stored in bank vaults.
clues.fact: A standard gold bar held by central banks weighs about 12.4 kg (400 troy ounces).

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Sticky amber pancake topping sold in a green tin with a lion on it; Brits pour it on porridge.
clues.fact: The Lyle's Golden Syrup tin is recognised by Guinness as the world's oldest unchanged brand packaging.

clues.label: Film
clues.clue: 1964 James Bond film whose villain, Auric, plots to raid Fort Knox; Shirley Bassey sang its theme.
clues.fact: In Goldfinger, a woman is famously found painted all over in gold.

themeHint: Think 25 December: Santa, presents and a decorated tree.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Grumpy green Dr. Seuss character with a heart too small, who steals Whoville's presents.
clues.fact: Dr. Seuss published 'How the Grinch Stole Christmas!' in 1957.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Big honking farm bird roasted for festive dinners before turkey; the Cratchits ate one in A Christmas Carol.
clues.fact: Roast goose was a traditional Christmas dinner in Britain before turkey became popular.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Santa's cave-like den in a shopping centre, where children queue to visit him.
clues.fact: Santa's grottos in department stores became popular in Britain in the late 1800s.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Wrapped item placed under the tree for someone you love.
clues.fact: Giving gifts at midwinter dates back to Roman festivals such as Saturnalia.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Spiced biscuit dough used to build little decorated houses and men.
clues.fact: Gingerbread is flavoured with ginger and often sweetened with molasses or honey.

clues.label: Decoration
clues.clue: Rope of tinsel, holly or pine hung around the tree or over the fireplace.
clues.fact: Evergreen garlands were used in midwinter celebrations long before Christmas trees.

themeHint: Think of Zeus and the other gods on Mount Olympus.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Super-strong hero, son of Zeus, who completed twelve impossible labours.
clues.fact: The Greeks called him Heracles; Hercules is the Roman version of his name.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Pegasus was a winged one of these.
clues.fact: In myth, Pegasus sprang from Medusa's neck when Perseus cut off her head.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Underworld of the dead in Greek myth, named after the god who ruled it.
clues.fact: Its gates were guarded by Cerberus, a monstrous three-headed dog.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Protective headgear; Hades owned a magic one that made its wearer invisible.
clues.fact: Ancient Greek hoplite soldiers often wore a bronze Corinthian-style one that covered most of the face.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Sweet golden food made by bees; myth says it fed baby Zeus in a cave on Crete.
clues.fact: Bees make it from flower nectar, and stored properly it can keep for an extremely long time.

clues.label: Monster
clues.clue: Many-headed water serpent: cut off one head and two grew back. Hercules killed it.
clues.fact: Hercules killed it as his second labour, with help from his nephew Iolaus.

themeHint: Old MacDonald had one, with cows, pigs and tractors.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Swiss storybook girl who goes to live with her grandfather and his goats in the Alps.
clues.fact: The novel was written by Johanna Spyri and published in the early 1880s.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Farm animal you ride, which lives in a stable and eats hay and oats.
clues.fact: Horses can doze standing up because their legs can lock in place.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Wooden shed where chickens sleep at night and lay their eggs.
clues.fact: Hens like to roost on raised perches at night, which helps keep them safe from foxes.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Long-handled tool for chopping weeds and loosening soil; rhymes with 'toe'.
clues.fact: It is one of the oldest farming tools, used in ancient Egypt and Mesopotamia.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Pink meat from a pig's back leg, often sliced into sandwiches.
clues.fact: Parma ham from Italy is salted and air-dried for many months.

clues.label: Season
clues.clue: Busy time when farmers gather in their ripe crops.
clues.fact: The full moon nearest the autumn equinox is called the Harvest Moon.

themeHint: Look up after a shower on a sunny day: red, orange, yellow, green...

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Greek goddess of the rainbow; the coloured part of your eye shares her name.
clues.fact: In Greek myth, Iris carried messages between the gods and humans.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Long-legged wading bird with a down-curved beak; ancient Egyptians held it sacred, and the scarlet kind is bright red.
clues.fact: The scarlet ibis is the national bird of Trinidad and Tobago.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: The 'Emerald Isle', famous for green fields, shamrocks and St Patrick's Day.
clues.fact: Its national day, St Patrick's Day, is celebrated on 17 March.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Coloured liquid that fills pens and printer cartridges.
clues.fact: Colour printers mix cyan, magenta and yellow to make most other colours.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Sweet coloured coating swirled on top of cupcakes and birthday cakes.
clues.fact: Royal icing, made with egg whites, sets hard and is often used on wedding cakes.

clues.label: Colour
clues.clue: Deep blue-violet shade that sits between blue and violet in the rainbow.
clues.fact: The dye was traditionally made from plants of the Indigofera family.

themeHint: The hottest season of the year: beaches, holidays and sunshine.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Boy in Greek myth who flew too close to the sun, so his wax wings melted.
clues.fact: His wings were made by his father, Daedalus, so they could escape from Crete.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Big green lizard that basks in the sun to warm its cold-blooded body.
clues.fact: Galapagos marine iguanas are the only lizards that swim and feed in the sea.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Spanish Mediterranean island famous for beaches and summer parties.
clues.fact: It is one of the Balearic Islands, along with Majorca and Menorca.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Blow-up pool toy, like a ring, lilo or giant flamingo, that you float on.
clues.fact: Inflatable lifejackets can fill in seconds using a small gas cartridge.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Frozen dessert that drips down your cone on a hot day.
clues.fact: Italian gelato is usually denser than other versions because less air is whipped in.

clues.label: Drink
clues.clue: Classic hot brew served cold with lemon slices; hugely popular in the southern USA.
clues.fact: Sweet tea served cold is a famous tradition in the southern United States.

themeHint: Hot, green and full of vines, monkeys and big cats.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Tarzan's sweetheart, who swings through the trees with him.
clues.fact: Tarzan was created by author Edgar Rice Burroughs in 1912.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Biggest wild cat of the Americas, covered in rosettes and prowling the rainforest.
clues.fact: It has one of the strongest bites of any big cat, strong enough to pierce turtle shells.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Indonesian island of volcanoes and rainforest; its name is also slang for coffee.
clues.fact: It is the only home of the critically endangered Javan rhinoceros.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Rugged 4x4 first built for US soldiers in the Second World War, great on muddy tracks.
clues.fact: The original was developed for the US Army during the Second World War.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: World's largest tree fruit, huge and spiky, grown in tropical Asia.
clues.fact: It is the national fruit of Bangladesh.

clues.label: Film
clues.clue: Film where a magical board game unleashes a stampeding wilderness into a town.
clues.fact: The 1995 original starred Robin Williams.

themeHint: Yo ho ho! Think treasure maps, eye patches and ships on the high seas.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Captain ___ Sparrow, the swaggering pirate played by Johnny Depp.
clues.fact: Pirates of the Caribbean was inspired by a Disneyland theme-park ride.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Stinging, see-through sea creature with no brain or bones, drifting near ships.
clues.fact: Jellyfish have no brain, heart or bones.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Caribbean island whose Port Royal was a pirate haven; home of reggae and Usain Bolt.
clues.fact: Much of Port Royal sank into the sea during an earthquake in 1692.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Black flag with a white skull and crossbones.
clues.fact: Different pirate captains flew their own versions of it with different designs.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Strips of dried, salted meat that keep for ages on long sea voyages.
clues.fact: The word comes from 'charqui', a Quechua word from South America.

clues.label: Treasure
clues.clue: Rubies, emeralds and diamonds heaped inside a buried treasure chest.
clues.fact: The British Crown Jewels are kept in the Tower of London.

themeHint: Land of the rising sun: sushi, Mount Fuji and Tokyo.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Pink, round Nintendo hero who swallows enemies to copy their powers.
clues.fact: Kirby was created by Masahiro Sakurai and first appeared in 1992 on the Game Boy.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Colourful ornamental carp kept in Japanese garden ponds.
clues.fact: Some prize-winning ones have sold for more than a million US dollars.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Japan's old imperial capital, famous for temples, geishas and the Golden Pavilion.
clues.fact: It was the home of the emperor for over a thousand years, until 1869.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Traditional long robe with wide sleeves, tied with an obi sash.
clues.fact: The word literally means 'thing to wear'.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Super-tender marbled Wagyu meat named after a port city; NBA star Bryant was named after it.
clues.fact: To carry the name, it must come from Tajima cattle raised in Hyogo Prefecture.

clues.label: Martial Art
clues.clue: Martial art of kicks, punches and coloured belts; its name means 'empty hand'.
clues.fact: It developed on Okinawa and made its Olympic debut at the Tokyo 2020 Games.

themeHint: The colour of grass, leaves and limes.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Banjo-playing frog who sings that it's not easy being green.
clues.fact: He was created by puppeteer Jim Henson in 1955.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Leaf-green insect related to the grasshopper, whose loud chirping fills North American summer nights.
clues.fact: Many katydids look so much like leaves that predators simply overlook them.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: London's royal botanic site, with huge Victorian glasshouses and millions of plants.
clues.fact: It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site with one of the world's largest collections of living plants.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Glowing green rock from Superman's home planet that takes away his powers.
clues.fact: It first appeared in the Superman radio show in 1943.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Curly leafy green vegetable, a cabbage cousin popular in smoothies and crisps.
clues.fact: It belongs to the same plant species as cabbage, broccoli and cauliflower.

clues.label: Fruit
clues.clue: Furry brown fruit with bright green flesh and tiny black seeds.
clues.fact: It was once called the Chinese gooseberry, as it originally came from China.

themeHint: The room where meals are cooked: pots, pans and a stove.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Nigella ___, British TV cook famous for indulgent recipes.
clues.fact: Her first book, How to Eat, came out in 1998.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Clawed shellfish that turns bright red when boiled in a pot.
clues.fact: Live lobsters are usually blue-green or brown; cooking turns their shells red.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Cool cupboard or small room for storing food, much like a pantry.
clues.fact: The word comes from an old French word linked to lard, as it was where meat and bacon were kept.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Deep, long-handled spoon for serving soup.
clues.fact: Steelworks use giant metal ladles to pour molten steel.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Baked Italian dish of flat pasta sheets layered with meat sauce and cheese.
clues.fact: Garfield the cartoon cat is famously obsessed with it.

clues.label: Meal
clues.clue: Midday meal eaten between breakfast and dinner.
clues.fact: The word 'lunch' is a shortened form of 'luncheon'.

themeHint: Where you'd find a shed, a lawn and flowerbeds.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Girl's name that is also a white flower; Harry Potter's mother had it.
clues.fact: Harry Potter's mother was Lily Potter, born Lily Evans.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Red spotted beetle that gardeners love because it eats aphids.
clues.fact: In North America it is usually called a ladybug.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Grassy patch outside a house that needs mowing every week in summer.
clues.fact: Lawns are made of grasses that can survive being cut short again and again.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Noisy hand-held machine that pushes fallen autumn foliage into a pile with a jet of air.
clues.fact: Many run on small two-stroke petrol engines, though battery-powered ones are now common.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Crunchy green salad leaf, such as iceberg or cos.
clues.fact: Cos lettuce is also known as romaine.

clues.label: Flower
clues.clue: Purple, sweet-smelling herb that bees love, used in soaps and perfumes.
clues.fact: It belongs to the mint family.

themeHint: Land of tacos, sombreros and the Aztecs.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Guitar-loving boy who visits the Land of the Dead in Pixar's film Coco.
clues.fact: Coco won the Oscar for Best Animated Feature.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Orange-and-black butterfly that flies thousands of kilometres to spend winter in Mexico's mountains.
clues.fact: Millions cluster together on fir trees in the mountains of central Mexico each winter.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Huge capital built on the ruins of the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan.
clues.fact: Mexico City stands where the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan was built on an island in a lake.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Pair of rattles shaken in time to Latin music, often made from gourds and seeds.
clues.fact: They are usually played in pairs, one in each hand.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Rich, dark sauce of chillies with a hint of chocolate; shares its name with a digging animal.
clues.fact: Both Puebla and Oaxaca claim to be the home of this famous sauce.

clues.label: Music
clues.clue: Strolling band in big sombreros, with trumpets, violins and guitars.
clues.fact: UNESCO added this musical tradition to its list of intangible cultural heritage in 2011.

themeHint: Six legs and creepy-crawly: think beetles, ants and flies.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Little Miss ___ sat on a tuffet, eating her curds and whey, till a spider came along.
clues.fact: The nursery rhyme was first printed in the early 1800s.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Whining biter that can spread malaria.
clues.fact: Only female mosquitoes bite, as they need blood to produce their eggs.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Tall earth tower built by termites on the African savanna.
clues.fact: Termite mounds have air channels that help keep the nest inside cool.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Curved lens on a handle for taking a closer look at tiny bugs.
clues.fact: On a sunny day it can focus sunlight enough to start a fire.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Yellow beetle larva fed to pet lizards and birds, and roasted as a crunchy snack.
clues.fact: Mealworms are the larvae of the darkling beetle.

clues.label: Insect
clues.clue: Green insect that holds its front legs together as if praying.
clues.fact: It can turn its head almost 180 degrees to look over its shoulder.

themeHint: When the sun goes down, the moon comes up and you go to bed.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Florence ___, the 'Lady with the Lamp', who cared for wounded soldiers on her rounds after dark.
clues.fact: Florence Nightingale is seen as the founder of modern nursing.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Bird that hoots and hunts in the dark; also a name for a person who stays up late.
clues.fact: Owls can turn their heads around about 270 degrees.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Top of the world in the Arctic, where winter brings months of darkness; Santa's home.
clues.fact: At the North Pole the sun sets once a year and stays down for about six months.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Small dim lamp left on so children aren't scared of the dark.
clues.fact: Many modern plug-in ones use LEDs and very little electricity.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Warm drink taken just before bed; also an old-fashioned sleeping hat.
clues.fact: Before central heating, people often wore cloth caps in bed to keep their heads warm.

clues.label: Word
clues.clue: Describes owls, bats and other animals that are active after dark.
clues.fact: Many desert animals are active at night to avoid the heat of the day.

themeHint: Grab some popcorn and watch the big screen.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Keanu Reeves' hero who takes the red pill in The Matrix; his name means 'new'.
clues.fact: The Matrix (1999) made 'bullet time' slow-motion effects famous.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Simba's lioness best friend in The Lion King.
clues.fact: Beyonce voiced her in the 2019 remake.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Magical land reached through the back of a wardrobe in C.S. Lewis's books.
clues.fact: The first Narnia book published was The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe in 1950.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Harry Potter's first racing broomstick, the ___ Two Thousand; also a dark rain cloud.
clues.fact: Nimbus is also the name for a dark rain cloud.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Cinema snack of tortilla chips smothered in melted cheese.
clues.fact: They are said to have been invented in Mexico in 1943 by Ignacio 'Nacho' Anaya.

clues.label: Film
clues.clue: Nickname of Nigeria's booming film industry, which makes more films each year than Hollywood.
clues.fact: Nollywood took off in the 1990s with straight-to-video films, and 1992's Living in Bondage is often called its first big hit.

themeHint: Think of the continent the Sahara and the Nile are on.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Masked Nigerian striker named African Footballer of the Year for 2023.
clues.fact: Victor Osimhen was named CAF African Footballer of the Year for 2023.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: The world's largest bird cannot fly but can outrun most animals on the savanna.
clues.fact: Ostriches lay the largest eggs of any living bird.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Green spot in the Sahara where water comes up from underground and palm trees grow.
clues.fact: Many desert oases grow date palms, which give both food and shade.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Tall, four-sided stone pillar with a pointed top, first carved in ancient Egypt.
clues.fact: Ancient Egyptian obelisks now stand in cities such as Rome, Paris, London and New York.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Green pod vegetable that turns soups slimy; loved in West African stews.
clues.fact: Okra is thought to have originated in Africa and is also known as ladies' fingers.

clues.label: Resource
clues.clue: 'Black gold' pumped from the ground in Nigeria, Angola and Libya and refined into petrol.
clues.fact: Nigeria is one of Africa's largest producers of crude oil.

themeHint: Think of labs, experiments, microscopes and test tubes.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Physicist who led the atomic bomb project; Cillian Murphy played him in a 2023 film.
clues.fact: The 2023 film about J. Robert Oppenheimer won the Oscar for Best Picture.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Scientists marvel at this clever eight-armed sea creature with three hearts.
clues.fact: An octopus has blue blood and can change colour in a fraction of a second.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Domed building with big telescopes for studying the stars.
clues.fact: Chile's dry Atacama Desert hosts some of the world's major telescopes thanks to its clear skies.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Metal cylinder of breathable gas carried by divers, climbers and astronauts.
clues.fact: Most climbers on Everest carry bottled oxygen because the air at the top is so thin.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Layered bulb that makes you cry; its thin skin is a classic first slide under school microscopes.
clues.fact: The skin cells of this vegetable are large and easy to see, which is why it is used in school labs.

clues.label: Space
clues.clue: Curved path a planet or moon follows around a bigger body, like Earth around the Sun.
clues.fact: Earth takes about 365 days to complete one orbit of the Sun.

themeHint: Think of the country of the Eiffel Tower, croissants and berets.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: French scientist who made a rabies vaccine; heat-treated milk is named after him.
clues.fact: Louis Pasteur developed early vaccines against rabies and anthrax.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Curly-coated dog, France's national dog, often given fancy pom-pom haircuts.
clues.fact: Despite its French fame, the poodle is believed to have originated in Germany as a water dog.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: City of light on the River Seine, home to the Louvre.
clues.fact: The Eiffel Tower was built for the 1889 World's Fair in this city.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: French car maker whose badge shows a lion; its 504 model was long a favourite on Nigerian roads.
clues.fact: Peugeot began as a family business making tools and coffee grinders before cars.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Flaky French breakfast pastry with a dark, sweet bar baked inside.
clues.fact: In south-west France this pastry is often called a chocolatine.

clues.label: Product
clues.clue: Scented liquid in a fancy bottle that France is famous for, such as Chanel No. 5.
clues.fact: The town of Grasse in southern France is often called the world's perfume capital.

themeHint: Think of the Amazon, the Andes and Brazilian football.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Brazilian football legend nicknamed O Rei, the King.
clues.fact: Pele is the only player to have won three FIFA World Cups.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Sharp-toothed fish of Amazon rivers, famous for feeding frenzies.
clues.fact: Many piranha species actually eat plants and seeds as well as meat.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Andean country home to Machu Picchu and Lima.
clues.fact: Lake Titicaca, on Peru's border with Bolivia, is one of the highest navigable lakes in the world.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Woollen blanket with a hole for your head, worn in the Andes.
clues.fact: Ponchos have been worn in the Andes since before the Spanish arrived.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Starchy tuber first farmed in the Andes; mashed, baked or fried into chips.
clues.fact: The potato was first domesticated in the Andes of present-day Peru and Bolivia.

clues.label: Region
clues.clue: Windswept land of glaciers and mountains at the southern tip of Argentina and Chile.
clues.fact: Patagonia's Torres del Paine and Perito Moreno Glacier draw visitors from around the world.

themeHint: Think of a colour that means stop, like blood or a fire engine.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Reindeer with a glowing nose who guided Santa's sleigh.
clues.fact: Rudolph first appeared in a 1939 booklet given away by a US department store.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Small garden bird with a bright red breast, a favourite on Christmas cards.
clues.fact: The European robin often follows gardeners to catch worms turned up by digging.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Narrow body of water between Africa and Arabia, linked to the Mediterranean by the Suez Canal.
clues.fact: The Suez Canal connects the Red Sea to the Mediterranean Sea.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Deep-red precious gemstone given on a 40th wedding anniversary.
clues.fact: Rubies and sapphires are both forms of the same mineral, corundum.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Soft red berry made of tiny juicy bumps, often made into jam.
clues.fact: A raspberry is made up of many small drupelets, each with its own seed.

clues.label: Flower
clues.clue: Thorny flower given in bunches on Valentine's Day.
clues.fact: The rose is the national flower of England and the United States.

themeHint: Think of animals that live in your home, like dogs, cats and goldfish.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Classic name for a pet dog that means 'wanderer'; NASA's Mars vehicles share it.
clues.fact: NASA's Mars vehicles are also called by this word, which means a wanderer.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Long-eared pet that lives in a hutch and nibbles carrots.
clues.fact: A rabbit's front teeth never stop growing.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Shelter where abandoned cats and dogs wait to be adopted (two words).
clues.fact: Battersea in London, founded in 1860, is one of the oldest animal shelters in the world.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Prize strip of fabric, often blue or red, pinned on the winner at a pet show.
clues.fact: At many American pet and farm shows, a blue ribbon means first place.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Dried grapes that are poisonous to dogs, so never share them.
clues.fact: Grapes and their dried form can cause kidney failure in dogs.

clues.label: Breed
clues.clue: Powerful black-and-tan German guard dog breed.
clues.fact: The breed is named after the German town of Rottweil.

themeHint: Think of capes, masks and saving the day.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Caped hero from Krypton who works as reporter Clark Kent.
clues.fact: This hero first appeared in Action Comics in 1938.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: A bite from one of these gave Peter Parker his powers.
clues.fact: Weight for weight, the silk of this creature can be stronger than steel.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Kansas farm town where Clark Kent grew up; its name sounds like a tiny village.
clues.fact: A TV series named after this town ran for ten seasons from 2001.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Captain America's round, star-marked piece of defensive kit.
clues.fact: Captain America first appeared in comics in 1941.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Leafy green that Popeye gulps from a can for super strength.
clues.fact: Spinach is rich in iron, but the iron is not easily absorbed by the body.

clues.label: Role
clues.clue: Helper who fights next to a hero, like Robin with Batman.
clues.fact: Robin first appeared alongside Batman in 1940.

themeHint: Think of kilts, bagpipes and the Loch Ness Monster.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Edinburgh-born actor who was the first James Bond on film (full name).
clues.fact: Sean Connery won an Oscar for his role in The Untouchables.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Tiny, sturdy horse breed from islands far north of the Scottish mainland.
clues.fact: Shetland ponies are among the strongest horses for their size.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Seaside town known as the home of golf, where Prince William went to university.
clues.fact: The University of St Andrews, founded in the 1400s, is Scotland's oldest university.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Machine improved by Scottish inventor James Watt that powered trains and factories.
clues.fact: James Watt made the steam engine far more efficient, and the unit of power, the watt, is named after him.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Crumbly, buttery biscuit, often sold in tartan tins.
clues.fact: Classic shortbread uses just three ingredients: butter, sugar and flour.

clues.label: Fish
clues.clue: Pink-fleshed fish that leaps up Scottish rivers to spawn.
clues.fact: Salmon return to the river where they hatched in order to breed.

themeHint: Think of 31 October: costumes, pumpkins and ghosts.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Director of Edward Scissorhands and The Nightmare Before Christmas (full name).
clues.fact: Tim Burton worked as an animator at Disney early in his career.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Big, hairy spider that makes a classic creepy costume prop.
clues.fact: Some female tarantulas can live for more than 20 years.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Region of Romania where Bram Stoker set Count Dracula's castle.
clues.fact: Bran Castle in this region is often marketed as Dracula's Castle.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Engraved stone marking a grave, a favourite spooky decoration.
clues.fact: Tombstone is also the name of a famous Wild West town in Arizona.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Fruit on a stick coated in hard caramel, a treat at autumn fairs.
clues.fact: In the US a similar treat is called a candy apple.

clues.label: Tradition
clues.clue: Children in costume knock on doors saying this three-word phrase.
clues.fact: Trick-or-treating became widespread in North America in the mid-1900s.

themeHint: Think small. Very small: mini, wee and teeny things.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Peter Pan's little fairy who sprinkles pixie dust.
clues.fact: Tinker Bell first appeared in J. M. Barrie's 1904 play Peter Pan.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Tiny eight-legged bloodsucker that clings to dogs and deer.
clues.fact: Ticks are arachnids, related to spiders rather than insects.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Pacific island nation, one of the world's smallest, that earns money from its '.tv' web address.
clues.fact: Tuvalu earns income by licensing its .tv internet domain.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Little metal cap that protects your fingertip when sewing.
clues.fact: Thimbles have been used for sewing since at least Roman times.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Spanish small plates shared with friends in bars.
clues.fact: Tapas comes from the Spanish verb tapar, meaning to cover.

clues.label: Measure
clues.clue: Smallest common kitchen spoon, used for sugar in tea.
clues.fact: In recipes, three of these spoons make one tablespoon.

themeHint: Think of a boot-shaped country.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Venetian composer of The Four Seasons, nicknamed the Red Priest.
clues.fact: Antonio Vivaldi was nicknamed the Red Priest because of his red hair.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Venomous snake with long folding fangs; Italy's only dangerous snakes are this kind.
clues.fact: Vipers have long hinged fangs that fold back when the mouth is closed.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Italian city of canals, gondolas and St Mark's Square.
clues.fact: Venice is built on more than 100 small islands in a lagoon.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Classic Italian scooter whose name means 'wasp'.
clues.fact: The Vespa was first launched by the Piaggio company in 1946.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Sour liquid; Modena's dark balsamic kind is aged in wooden barrels.
clues.fact: Traditional balsamic from Modena must be aged for at least 12 years.

clues.label: Volcano
clues.clue: Volcano that buried Pompeii in AD 79, still towering over Naples.
clues.fact: The eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79 also buried the nearby town of Herculaneum.

themeHint: Think of hearts and 14 February.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Saint whose feast day on 14 February is for sweethearts.
clues.fact: Saint Valentine's Day became linked with romance in the Middle Ages.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Small mouse-like rodent; prairie ones pair up for life. Rhymes with 'hole'.
clues.fact: Prairie voles are among the few mammals that form lifelong pair bonds.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Italian city where Shakespeare set Romeo and Juliet.
clues.fact: Tourists in this city visit a balcony said to be Juliet's.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Sheer fabric covering a bride's face on her wedding day.
clues.fact: Wedding veils date back to ancient Rome.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Sweet flavour from orchid pods, used in wedding cakes and ice cream.
clues.fact: Vanilla comes from the pods of an orchid native to Mexico.

clues.label: Flower
clues.clue: Roses are red, these are blue, sugar is sweet, and so are you.
clues.fact: Violets are edible and are sometimes candied to decorate cakes.

themeHint: Think of 'once upon a time' and 'happily ever after'.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Girl who flies to Neverland with Peter Pan and the Lost Boys.
clues.fact: The name Wendy became popular after Peter Pan was first staged in 1904.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Big bad creature who blew down houses and tricked Red Riding Hood.
clues.fact: Wolves live and hunt in family groups called packs.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Strange land Alice reaches by falling down a rabbit hole.
clues.fact: Lewis Carroll wrote Alice's Adventures in Wonderland for a real girl named Alice Liddell.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Stick a fairy godmother waves to work her magic.
clues.fact: Cinderella's fairy godmother turns a pumpkin into a coach.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Hard, brain-shaped nut whose shell became tiny Thumbelina's cradle.
clues.fact: In Andersen's tale, Thumbelina's cradle is a polished walnut shell.

clues.label: Character
clues.clue: Wicked old woman who lured Hansel and Gretel into her gingerbread house.
clues.fact: Hansel and Gretel was collected by the Brothers Grimm and first published in 1812.

themeHint: Think of songs, singers and dancing.

clues.label: Name
clues.clue: Lagos-born Afrobeats star who sang on Drake's hit One Dance.
clues.fact: Wizkid won a Grammy in 2021 for Brown Skin Girl, his song with Beyoncé, Blue Ivy and Saint Jhn.

clues.label: Animal
clues.clue: Humpback types of this ocean giant sing long, haunting songs.
clues.fact: Male humpbacks sing complex songs that change gradually over the years.

clues.label: Place
clues.clue: Famous 1969 hippie music festival on a New York farm; also Snoopy's little bird friend.
clues.fact: The festival was held in Bethel, New York, some distance from the town it was named after.

clues.label: Thing
clues.clue: Small instrument a referee blows to stop play.
clues.fact: A tin version of this instrument is common in Irish folk music.

clues.label: Food
clues.clue: Juicy fruit in a Grammy-winning Harry Styles song, '___ Sugar'.
clues.fact: Watermelon Sugar won Harry Styles a Grammy for Best Pop Solo Performance.

clues.label: Dance
clues.clue: Elegant ballroom dance in three-four time, loved in Vienna.
clues.fact: Johann Strauss II wrote The Blue Danube, a famous piece in this dance style.
